title: Gomez's Hamburger
caption: Gomez's Hamburger, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Gomez's Hamburger, IRAS 18059-3211 · constellation Sagittarius · about 1600 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two glowing “buns” sandwich a dark “patty” in this Hubble image, and it's easy to see how the object earned its nickname, Gomez's Hamburger. It surrounds a Sun-like star near the end of its life.

The star has already thrown off large amounts of gas and dust. The bright upper and lower halves are starlight reflecting off that dust, while the dark band across the middle is a thick lane of dust seen edge-on, hiding the star behind it.

What we are watching is a star on its way to becoming a planetary nebula. In time, the gas around it should begin to glow in color, as the exposed core heats it. For now, Gomez's Hamburger is a snapshot of the short, dusty stage before that happens.

understand.summary: Hubble's WFPC2 camera observed through blue B, visual V and red R filters. ESA/Hubble does not say which color each was given.
understand.eye: The nebula is far too small and faint to see by eye; what lights it is reflected starlight.
